transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. How can I help you today?

I'm here because... well, I had an incident at work. I snapped on a board call over some minor question about the facility budget. That's... it's just not how I run my company. Or how I treat people. So, I thought I should get it checked out.
Have you had other moments recently where you felt unusually upset, anxious, or had trouble managing your emotions?

I suppose so. It's just... things that usually settle me down aren't working. Like working on a chess problem, or going over my hiking notes. Even just having dinner with my wife. They all just feel... flat right now. Like I know I should be enjoying them, but I just... I can't seem to get there.
Have you noticed that you’ve lost interest in activities you used to enjoy, like chess, hiking, or spending time with your wife?
Yes. That's... pretty much what I just said. I just don't have the interest for them at the moment.
Have you been feeling like you’re not good enough or blaming yourself for things more than usual lately?
No... not really. I know what I'm capable of, and I know how to do my job. I wouldn't say I feel like I'm not good enough. It's just... what I mentioned before. The temper.
Have you been feeling down, depressed, or hopeless most of the time lately?
No... I wouldn't use those words. I'm not... hopeless. Just... like I said, things are a bit flat right now.
How long have you felt this way about activities like chess, hiking, or spending time with your wife — has it been most days, and for how many weeks or months?
It's been about six days. Just... ever since the explosion. The fire, during that walkthrough. That's when it started.
Can you tell me more about the explosion and fire during the walkthrough — how intense was the situation, and how did you feel during and after it happened?

It was... just an explosion. A fire. Exactly what it sounds like. 

I don't really want to get into the whole play-by-play of it. We were doing the walkthrough, it happened, and... we had to get out. I just did what needed to be done. I don't really know what else to tell you about it.
Would you say that the explosion and fire during the walkthrough felt traumatic to you at the time?
Traumatic? I... I don't know if I'd use that word. It was an emergency. A bad situation. I was just focused on getting out of there. I wasn't really... sitting around feeling things about it.
Can you describe what happened during the explosion and fire on the walkthrough, and how you reacted to it at the time?

I... look, I feel like I just answered that. I really don't want to go through the whole play-by-play again. 

It blew up, there was fire, and we left. As for how I reacted... I just did what I had to do to get us out of there. There wasn't time to stand around reacting. I don't really see the point in digging into the exact details of it.
Since the explosion and fire, have you been avoiding certain places, people, or activities that remind you of what happened?

I haven't gone back to the new building. There's no reason for me to be there right now anyway. 

And... the paperwork. The mortgage folder, the safety reports... they're on my desk. I just... I haven't opened them. Every time I go to grab them, my stomach just drops. So I leave them be. That's all.
Since the explosion and fire, have you found yourself thinking about it when you didn’t want to, or has it been coming back to you in ways that upset you?

I guess... yeah. Sometimes. I'll just be in the middle of a phone call, or looking at some numbers. And the blast, that fire by the loading area... it just jumps back into my head. It's like some bad film I didn't ask to see. That's about it.
Since the explosion and fire, have you been more irritable, easily startled, or had trouble sleeping or concentrating?

I don't know about all that. I guess... maybe I've been a little jumpy. 

Like, if a door shuts hard in the office, or... if the printer kicks on behind me... I jump. Just for a second, it feels like something went off again. Then it takes me a few minutes to get my hands steady. But that's about it.
Have you noticed that you've been feeling more down, upset, or emotionally numb in general since the fire, even when you're not thinking about it directly?

I don't know about numb. Just... things feel a bit flat. 

Usually, if I need to settle down, I'll look at a chess problem, or go over my notes for a hiking trip. Or just sit down for dinner with my wife. But lately... I know I'm supposed to be enjoying those things, but I just can't seem to get there. It's just... flat.
Since the fire, have you noticed any days where you felt especially overwhelmed or emotionally reactive, even to small things that wouldn't usually bother you?

I suppose... yeah. That's actually why I'm here. 

I was on a board call the other day. Someone asked a pretty standard question about the facility budget, and I... I snapped at them. Just lost my temper over nothing. That's not how I run my company. It's not how I treat my people. I don't know where it came from.
Since the fire, have you noticed a significant decrease in your energy or motivation, even for tasks or activities you used to handle without trouble?

No... I don't think so. I still get up and do what needs doing every day. My drive is the same as it's always been. It's just... well, what I said a minute ago about the temper. But no, my energy is fine.
Have you had any unwanted or upsetting memories of the fire coming back to you repeatedly, or felt as if you were reliving the event in any way?

Yeah... I suppose. 

Sometimes I'll just be working. In the middle of a call, or... just looking at the numbers. And out of nowhere, the blast, or that fire by the loading area... it just jumps back into my head. 

It's like some bad film I didn't ask to see. Just flashes like that.
Since the fire, have you noticed any physical reactions — like a racing heart, sweating, or feeling very tense — when you're reminded of the explosion or something similar to it?
No... not really. My heart's fine. I don't get the sweats or anything like that. It's just... just what I told you. Physically, I'm fine.
Since the fire, have you found yourself feeling unusually angry or irritable on a regular basis, even outside of specific stressful moments?

Well... yeah. Like I mentioned before. That's honestly why I'm here. 

We had a board call recently. Someone asked a really small question about the facility budget, and I just... I snapped on them. Completely lost my temper. 

And... well, I don't do that. That is not how I run my company, and it's not how I treat people. So... yes. I guess I have been.
